# <span class="secnum">23</span> Indexed Collections

# <span class="secnum">23.1</span> Array Objects

Arrays are [exotic objects](#exotic-object) that give special treatment
to a certain class of [property names](#property-name). See
[10.4.2](#sec-array-exotic-objects) for a definition of this special
treatment.

# <span class="secnum">23.1.1</span> The Array Constructor

The Array [constructor](#constructor):

- is <span class="dfn" tabindex="-1">%Array%</span>.
- is the initial value of the "Array" property of the [global
  object](#sec-global-object).
- creates and initializes a new Array when called as a
  [constructor](#constructor).
- also creates and initializes a new Array when called as a function
  rather than as a [constructor](#constructor). Thus the function call
  `Array(…)` is equivalent to the object creation expression
  `new Array(…)` with the same arguments.
- is a function whose behaviour differs based upon the number and types
  of its arguments.
- may be used as the value of an `extends` clause of a class definition.
  Subclass [constructors](#constructor) that intend to inherit the
  exotic Array behaviour must include a `super` call to the Array
  [constructor](#constructor) to initialize subclass instances that are
  [Array exotic objects](#array-exotic-object). However, most of the
  `Array.prototype` methods are generic methods that are not dependent
  upon their this value being an [Array exotic
  object](#array-exotic-object).

<span id="sec-array-items"></span><span id="sec-array-len"></span><span id="sec-array-constructor-array"></span>

# <span class="secnum">23.1.1.1</span> Array ( ...`values` )

This function performs the following steps when called:

1.  If NewTarget is undefined, let `newTarget` be the [active function
    object](#active-function-object); else let `newTarget` be NewTarget.
2.  Let `proto` be ? <a href="#sec-getprototypefromconstructor"
    class="e-user-code">GetPrototypeFromConstructor</a>(`newTarget`,
    "%Array.prototype%").
3.  Let `numberOfArgs` be the number of elements in `values`.
4.  If `numberOfArgs` = 0, return ! [ArrayCreate](#sec-arraycreate)(0,
    `proto`).
5.  If `numberOfArgs` = 1, then
    1.  Let `len` be `values`\[0\].
    2.  Let `array` be ! [ArrayCreate](#sec-arraycreate)(0, `proto`).
    3.  If `len` [is not a
        Number](#sec-ecmascript-language-types-number-type), then
        1.  Perform
            ! [CreateDataPropertyOrThrow](#sec-createdatapropertyorthrow)(`array`,
            "0", `len`).
        2.  Let `intLen` be 1<sub>𝔽</sub>.
    4.  Else,
        1.  Let `intLen` be ! [ToUint32](#sec-touint32)(`len`).
        2.  If [SameValueZero](#sec-samevaluezero)(`intLen`, `len`) is
            false, throw a RangeError exception.
    5.  Perform ! [Set](#sec-set-o-p-v-throw)(`array`, "length",
        `intLen`, true).
    6.  Return `array`.
6.  [Assert](#assert): `numberOfArgs` ≥ 2.
7.  Let `array` be ? [ArrayCreate](#sec-arraycreate)(`numberOfArgs`,
    `proto`).
8.  Let `k` be 0.
9.  Repeat, while `k` \< `numberOfArgs`,
    1.  Let `Pk` be ! [ToString](#sec-tostring)([𝔽](#𝔽)(`k`)).
    2.  Let `itemK` be `values`\[`k`\].
    3.  Perform
        ! [CreateDataPropertyOrThrow](#sec-createdatapropertyorthrow)(`array`,
        `Pk`, `itemK`).
    4.  Set `k` to `k` + 1.
10. [Assert](#assert): The [mathematical value
    of](#mathematical-value-of) `array`'s "length" property is
    `numberOfArgs`.
11. Return `array`.

# <span class="secnum">23.1.2</span> Properties of the Array Constructor

The Array [constructor](#constructor):

- has a `[[Prototype]]` internal slot whose value is
  [%Function.prototype%](#sec-properties-of-the-function-prototype-object).
- has a "length" property whose value is 1<sub>𝔽</sub>.
- has the following properties:

# <span class="secnum">23.1.2.1</span> Array.from ( `items` \[ , `mapper` \[ , `thisArg` \] \] )

This function performs the following steps when called:

1.  Let `C` be the this value.
2.  If `mapper` is undefined, then
    1.  Let `mapping` be false.
3.  Else,
    1.  If [IsCallable](#sec-iscallable)(`mapper`) is false, throw a
        TypeError exception.
    2.  Let `mapping` be true.
4.  Let `usingIterator` be
    ? <a href="#sec-getmethod" class="e-user-code">GetMethod</a>(`items`,
    [%Symbol.iterator%](#sec-well-known-symbols)).
5.  If `usingIterator` is not undefined, then
    1.  If [IsConstructor](#sec-isconstructor)(`C`) is true, then
        1.  Let `A` be
            ? <a href="#sec-construct" class="e-user-code">Construct</a>(`C`).
    2.  Else,
        1.  Let `A` be ! [ArrayCreate](#sec-arraycreate)(0).
    3.  Let `iteratorRecord` be ? <a href="#sec-getiteratorfrommethod"
        class="e-user-code">GetIteratorFromMethod</a>(`items`,
        `usingIterator`).
    4.  Let `k` be 0.
    5.  Repeat,
        1.  If `k` ≥ 2<sup>53</sup> - 1, then
            1.  Let `error` be [ThrowCompletion](#sec-throwcompletion)(a
                newly created TypeError object).
            2.  Return
                ? <a href="#sec-iteratorclose" class="e-user-code">IteratorClose</a>(`iteratorRecord`,
                `error`).
        2.  Let `Pk` be ! [ToString](#sec-tostring)([𝔽](#𝔽)(`k`)).
        3.  Let `next` be ? <a href="#sec-iteratorstepvalue"
            class="e-user-code">IteratorStepValue</a>(`iteratorRecord`).
        4.  If `next` is done, then
            1.  Perform
                ? <a href="#sec-set-o-p-v-throw" class="e-user-code">Set</a>(`A`,
                "length", [𝔽](#𝔽)(`k`), true).
            2.  Return `A`.
        5.  If `mapping` is true, then
            1.  Let `mappedValue` be
                [Completion](#sec-completion-ao)(<a href="#sec-call" class="e-user-code">Call</a>(`mapper`,
                `thisArg`, « `next`, [𝔽](#𝔽)(`k`) »)).
            2.  <a href="#sec-ifabruptcloseiterator"
                class="e-user-code">IfAbruptCloseIterator</a>(`mappedValue`,
                `iteratorRecord`).
        6.  Else,
            1.  Let `mappedValue` be `next`.
        7.  Let `defineStatus` be
            [Completion](#sec-completion-ao)(<a href="#sec-createdatapropertyorthrow"
            class="e-user-code">CreateDataPropertyOrThrow</a>(`A`, `Pk`,
            `mappedValue`)).
        8.  <a href="#sec-ifabruptcloseiterator"
            class="e-user-code">IfAbruptCloseIterator</a>(`defineStatus`,
            `iteratorRecord`).
        9.  Set `k` to `k` + 1.
6.  [NOTE](#note-step): `items` is not
    [iterable](#sec-iterable-interface) so assume it is an [array-like
    object](#sec-lengthofarraylike).
7.  Let `arrayLike` be ! [ToObject](#sec-toobject)(`items`).
8.  Let `len` be ? <a href="#sec-lengthofarraylike"
    class="e-user-code">LengthOfArrayLike</a>(`arrayLike`).
9.  If [IsConstructor](#sec-isconstructor)(`C`) is true, then
    1.  Let `A` be
        ? <a href="#sec-construct" class="e-user-code">Construct</a>(`C`,
        « [𝔽](#𝔽)(`len`) »).
10. Else,
    1.  Let `A` be ? [ArrayCreate](#sec-arraycreate)(`len`).
11. Let `k` be 0.
12. Repeat, while `k` \< `len`,
    1.  Let `Pk` be ! [ToString](#sec-tostring)([𝔽](#𝔽)(`k`)).
    2.  Let `kValue` be
        ? <a href="#sec-get-o-p" class="e-user-code">Get</a>(`arrayLike`,
        `Pk`).
    3.  If `mapping` is true, then
        1.  Let `mappedValue` be
            ? <a href="#sec-call" class="e-user-code">Call</a>(`mapper`,
            `thisArg`, « `kValue`, [𝔽](#𝔽)(`k`) »).
    4.  Else,
        1.  Let `mappedValue` be `kValue`.
    5.  Perform ? <a href="#sec-createdatapropertyorthrow"
        class="e-user-code">CreateDataPropertyOrThrow</a>(`A`, `Pk`,
        `mappedValue`).
    6.  Set `k` to `k` + 1.
13. Perform
    ? <a href="#sec-set-o-p-v-throw" class="e-user-code">Set</a>(`A`,
    "length", [𝔽](#𝔽)(`len`), true).
14. Return `A`.

<span class="note">Note</span>

<div class="note-contents">

This method is an intentionally generic factory method; it does not
require that its this value be the Array [constructor](#constructor).
Therefore it can be transferred to or inherited by any other
[constructors](#constructor) that may be called with a single numeric
argument.

</div>

# <span class="secnum">23.1.2.2</span> Array.fromAsync ( `items` \[ , `mapper` \[ , `thisArg` \] \] )

This async function performs the following steps when called:

1.  Let `C` be the this value.
2.  Let `mapping` be false.
3.  If `mapper` is not undefined, then
    1.  If [IsCallable](#sec-iscallable)(`mapper`) is false, throw a
        TypeError exception.
    2.  Set `mapping` to true.
4.  Let `iteratorRecord` be undefined.
5.  Let `usingAsyncIterator` be
    ? <a href="#sec-getmethod" class="e-user-code">GetMethod</a>(`items`,
    [%Symbol.asyncIterator%](#sec-well-known-symbols)).
6.  If `usingAsyncIterator` is undefined, then
    1.  Let `usingSyncIterator` be
        ? <a href="#sec-getmethod" class="e-user-code">GetMethod</a>(`items`,
        [%Symbol.iterator%](#sec-well-known-symbols)).
    2.  If `usingSyncIterator` is not undefined, then
        1.  Set `iteratorRecord` to
            [CreateAsyncFromSyncIterator](#sec-createasyncfromsynciterator)(?
            <a href="#sec-getiteratorfrommethod"
            class="e-user-code">GetIteratorFromMethod</a>(`items`,
            `usingSyncIterator`)).
7.  Else,
    1.  Set `iteratorRecord` to ? <a href="#sec-getiteratorfrommethod"
        class="e-user-code">GetIteratorFromMethod</a>(`items`,
        `usingAsyncIterator`).
8.  If `iteratorRecord` is not undefined, then
    1.  If [IsConstructor](#sec-isconstructor)(`C`) is true, then
        1.  Let `A` be
            ? <a href="#sec-construct" class="e-user-code">Construct</a>(`C`).
    2.  Else,
        1.  Let `A` be ! [ArrayCreate](#sec-arraycreate)(0).
    3.  Let `k` be 0.
    4.  Repeat,
        1.  If `k` ≥ 2<sup>53</sup> - 1, then
            1.  Let `error` be [ThrowCompletion](#sec-throwcompletion)(a
                newly created TypeError object).
            2.  Return ? <a href="#sec-asynciteratorclose"
                class="e-user-code">AsyncIteratorClose</a>(`iteratorRecord`,
                `error`).
        2.  Let `Pk` be ! [ToString](#sec-tostring)([𝔽](#𝔽)(`k`)).
        3.  Let `nextResult` be
            ? <a href="#sec-call" class="e-user-code">Call</a>(`iteratorRecord`.`[[NextMethod]]`,
            `iteratorRecord`.`[[Iterator]]`).
        4.  Set `nextResult` to
            ? <a href="#await" class="e-user-code">Await</a>(`nextResult`).
        5.  If `nextResult` [is not an Object](#sec-object-type), throw
            a TypeError exception.
        6.  Let `done` be
            ? <a href="#sec-iteratorcomplete" class="e-user-code">IteratorComplete</a>(`nextResult`).
        7.  If `done` is true, then
            1.  Perform
                ? <a href="#sec-set-o-p-v-throw" class="e-user-code">Set</a>(`A`,
                "length", [𝔽](#𝔽)(`k`), true).
            2.  Return `A`.
        8.  Let `nextValue` be
            ? <a href="#sec-iteratorvalue" class="e-user-code">IteratorValue</a>(`nextResult`).
        9.  If `mapping` is true, then
            1.  Let `mappedValue` be
                [Completion](#sec-completion-ao)(<a href="#sec-call" class="e-user-code">Call</a>(`mapper`,
                `thisArg`, « `nextValue`, [𝔽](#𝔽)(`k`) »)).
            2.  <a href="#sec-ifabruptcloseasynciterator"
                class="e-user-code">IfAbruptCloseAsyncIterator</a>(`mappedValue`,
                `iteratorRecord`).
            3.  Set `mappedValue` to
                [Completion](#sec-completion-ao)(<a href="#await" class="e-user-code">Await</a>(`mappedValue`)).
            4.  <a href="#sec-ifabruptcloseasynciterator"
                class="e-user-code">IfAbruptCloseAsyncIterator</a>(`mappedValue`,
                `iteratorRecord`).
        10. Else,
            1.  Let `mappedValue` be `nextValue`.
        11. Let `defineStatus` be
            [Completion](#sec-completion-ao)(<a href="#sec-createdatapropertyorthrow"
            class="e-user-code">CreateDataPropertyOrThrow</a>(`A`, `Pk`,
            `mappedValue`)).
        12. <a href="#sec-ifabruptcloseasynciterator"
            class="e-user-code">IfAbruptCloseAsyncIterator</a>(`defineStatus`,
            `iteratorRecord`).
        13. Set `k` to `k` + 1.
9.  Else,
    1.  [NOTE](#note-step): `items` is neither [async
        iterable](#sec-asynciterable-interface) nor
        [iterable](#sec-iterable-interface) so assume it is an
        [array-like object](#sec-lengthofarraylike).
    2.  Let `arrayLike` be ! [ToObject](#sec-toobject)(`items`).
    3.  Let `len` be ? <a href="#sec-lengthofarraylike"
        class="e-user-code">LengthOfArrayLike</a>(`arrayLike`).
    4.  If [IsConstructor](#sec-isconstructor)(`C`) is true, then
        1.  Let `A` be
            ? <a href="#sec-construct" class="e-user-code">Construct</a>(`C`,
            « [𝔽](#𝔽)(`len`) »).
    5.  Else,
        1.  Let `A` be ? [ArrayCreate](#sec-arraycreate)(`len`).
    6.  Let `k` be 0.
    7.  Repeat, while `k` \< `len`,
        1.  Let `Pk` be ! [ToString](#sec-tostring)([𝔽](#𝔽)(`k`)).
        2.  Let `kValue` be
            ? <a href="#sec-get-o-p" class="e-user-code">Get</a>(`arrayLike`,
            `Pk`).
        3.  Set `kValue` to
            ? <a href="#await" class="e-user-code">Await</a>(`kValue`).
        4.  If `mapping` is true, then
            1.  Let `mappedValue` be
                ? <a href="#sec-call" class="e-user-code">Call</a>(`mapper`,
                `thisArg`, « `kValue`, [𝔽](#𝔽)(`k`) »).
            2.  Set `mappedValue` to
                ? <a href="#await" class="e-user-code">Await</a>(`mappedValue`).
        5.  Else,
            1.  Let `mappedValue` be `kValue`.
        6.  Perform ? <a href="#sec-createdatapropertyorthrow"
            class="e-user-code">CreateDataPropertyOrThrow</a>(`A`, `Pk`,
            `mappedValue`).
        7.  Set `k` to `k` + 1.
    8.  Perform
        ? <a href="#sec-set-o-p-v-throw" class="e-user-code">Set</a>(`A`,
        "length", [𝔽](#𝔽)(`len`), true).
    9.  Return `A`.

<span class="note">Note</span>

<div class="note-contents">

This method is an intentionally generic factory method; it does not
require that its this value be the Array [constructor](#constructor).
Therefore it can be transferred to or inherited by any other
[constructors](#constructor) that may be called with a single numeric
argument.

</div>

# <span class="secnum">23.1.2.3</span> Array.isArray ( `arg` )

This function performs the following steps when called:

1.  Return ? [IsArray](#sec-isarray)(`arg`).

# <span class="secnum">23.1.2.4</span> Array.of ( ...`items` )

This method performs the following steps when called:

1.  Let `len` be the number of elements in `items`.
2.  Let `lenNumber` be [𝔽](#𝔽)(`len`).
3.  Let `C` be the this value.
4.  If [IsConstructor](#sec-isconstructor)(`C`) is true, then
    1.  Let `A` be
        ? <a href="#sec-construct" class="e-user-code">Construct</a>(`C`,
        « `lenNumber` »).
5.  Else,
    1.  Let `A` be ? [ArrayCreate](#sec-arraycreate)(`len`).
6.  Let `k` be 0.
7.  Repeat, while `k` \< `len`,
    1.  Let `kValue` be `items`\[`k`\].
    2.  Let `Pk` be ! [ToString](#sec-tostring)([𝔽](#𝔽)(`k`)).
    3.  Perform ? <a href="#sec-createdatapropertyorthrow"
        class="e-user-code">CreateDataPropertyOrThrow</a>(`A`, `Pk`,
        `kValue`).
    4.  Set `k` to `k` + 1.
8.  Perform
    ? <a href="#sec-set-o-p-v-throw" class="e-user-code">Set</a>(`A`,
    "length", `lenNumber`, true).
9.  Return `A`.

<span class="note">Note</span>

<div class="note-contents">

This method is an intentionally generic factory method; it does not
require that its this value be the Array [constructor](#constructor).
Therefore it can be transferred to or inherited by other
[constructors](#constructor) that may be called with a single numeric
argument.

</div>

# <span class="secnum">23.1.2.5</span> Array.prototype

The value of `Array.prototype` is the [Array prototype
object](#sec-properties-of-the-array-prototype-object).

This property has the attributes { `[[Writable]]`: false,
`[[Enumerable]]`: false, `[[Configurable]]`: false }.

<span id="sec-get-array-@@species"></span>

# <span class="secnum">23.1.2.6</span> get Array \[ %Symbol.species% \]

`Array[%Symbol.species%]` is an [accessor property](#sec-object-type)
whose set accessor function is undefined. Its get accessor function
performs the following steps when called:

1.  Return the this value.

The value of the "name" property of this function is "get
\[Symbol.species\]".

<span class="note">Note</span>

<div class="note-contents">

Array prototype methods normally use their this value's
[constructor](#constructor) to create a derived object. However, a
subclass [constructor](#constructor) may over-ride that default
behaviour by redefining its [%Symbol.species%](#sec-well-known-symbols)
property.

</div>

# <span class="secnum">23.1.3</span> Properties of the Array Prototype Object

The <span class="dfn" tabindex="-1">Array prototype object</span>:

- is <span class="dfn" tabindex="-1">%Array.prototype%</span>.
- is an [Array exotic object](#array-exotic-object) and has the internal
  methods specified for such objects.
- has a "length" property whose initial value is +0<sub>𝔽</sub> and
  whose attributes are { `[[Writable]]`: true, `[[Enumerable]]`: false,
  `[[Configurable]]`: false }.
- has a `[[Prototype]]` internal slot whose value is
  [%Object.prototype%](#sec-properties-of-the-object-prototype-object).

<span class="note">Note</span>

<div class="note-contents">

The Array prototype object is specified to be an [Array exotic
object](#array-exotic-object) to ensure compatibility with ECMAScript
code that was created prior to the ECMAScript 2015 specification.

</div>

# <span class="secnum">23.1.3.1</span> Array.prototype.at ( `index` )

1.  Let `O` be ? [ToObject](#sec-toobject)(this value).
2.  Let `len` be ? <a href="#sec-lengthofarraylike"
    class="e-user-code">LengthOfArrayLike</a>(`O`).
3.  Let `relativeIndex` be ? <a href="#sec-tointegerorinfinity"
    class="e-user-code">ToIntegerOrInfinity</a>(`index`).
4.  If `relativeIndex` ≥ 0, then
    1.  Let `k` be `relativeIndex`.
5.  Else,
    1.  Let `k` be `len` + `relativeIndex`.
6.  If `k` \< 0 or `k` ≥ `len`, return undefined.
7.  Return ? <a href="#sec-get-o-p" class="e-user-code">Get</a>(`O`,
    ! [ToString](#sec-tostring)([𝔽](#𝔽)(`k`))).

# <span class="secnum">23.1.3.2</span> Array.prototype.concat ( ...`items` )

This method returns an array containing the array elements of the object
followed by the array elements of each argument.

It performs the following steps when called:

1.  Let `O` be ? [ToObject](#sec-toobject)(this value).
2.  Let `A` be ? <a href="#sec-arrayspeciescreate"
    class="e-user-code">ArraySpeciesCreate</a>(`O`, 0).
3.  Let `n` be 0.
4.  Prepend `O` to `items`.
5.  For each element `E` of `items`, do
    1.  Let `spreadable` be ? <a href="#sec-isconcatspreadable"
        class="e-user-code">IsConcatSpreadable</a>(`E`).
    2.  If `spreadable` is true, then
        1.  Let `len` be ? <a href="#sec-lengthofarraylike"
            class="e-user-code">LengthOfArrayLike</a>(`E`).
        2.  If `n` + `len` \> 2<sup>53</sup> - 1, throw a TypeError
            exception.
        3.  Let `k` be 0.
        4.  Repeat, while `k` \< `len`,
            1.  Let `Pk` be ! [ToString](#sec-tostring)([𝔽](#𝔽)(`k`)).
            2.  Let `exists` be
                ? <a href="#sec-hasproperty" class="e-user-code">HasProperty</a>(`E`,
                `Pk`).
            3.  If `exists` is true, then
                1.  Let `subElement` be
                    ? <a href="#sec-get-o-p" class="e-user-code">Get</a>(`E`,
                    `Pk`).
                2.  Perform ? <a href="#sec-createdatapropertyorthrow"
                    class="e-user-code">CreateDataPropertyOrThrow</a>(`A`,
                    ! [ToString](#sec-tostring)([𝔽](#𝔽)(`n`)),
                    `subElement`).
            4.  Set `n` to `n` + 1.
            5.  Set `k` to `k` + 1.
    3.  Else,
        1.  [NOTE](#note-step): `E` is added as a single item rather
            than spread.
        2.  If `n` ≥ 2<sup>53</sup> - 1, throw a TypeError exception.
        3.  Perform ? <a href="#sec-createdatapropertyorthrow"
            class="e-user-code">CreateDataPropertyOrThrow</a>(`A`,
            ! [ToString](#sec-tostring)([𝔽](#𝔽)(`n`)), `E`).
        4.  Set `n` to `n` + 1.
6.  <span id="step-array-proto-concat-set-length">Perform
    ? <a href="#sec-set-o-p-v-throw" class="e-user-code">Set</a>(`A`,
    "length", [𝔽](#𝔽)(`n`), true).</span>
7.  Return `A`.

The "length" property of this method is 1<sub>𝔽</sub>.

<span class="note">Note 1</span>

<div class="note-contents">

The explicit setting of the "length" property in step
[6](#step-array-proto-concat-set-length) is intended to ensure the
length is correct when the final non-empty element of `items` has
trailing holes or when `A` is not a built-in Array.

</div>

<span class="note">Note 2</span>

<div class="note-contents">

This method is intentionally generic; it does not require that its this
value be an Array. Therefore it can be transferred to other kinds of
objects for use as a method.

</div>

# <span class="secnum">23.1.3.2.1</span> IsConcatSpreadable ( `O` )

The abstract operation IsConcatSpreadable takes argument `O` (an
[ECMAScript language value](#sec-ecmascript-language-types)) and returns
either a [normal completion
containing](#sec-completion-record-specification-type) a Boolean or a
[throw completion](#sec-completion-record-specification-type). It
performs the following steps when called:

1.  If `O` [is not an Object](#sec-object-type), return false.
2.  Let `spreadable` be
    ? <a href="#sec-get-o-p" class="e-user-code">Get</a>(`O`,
    [%Symbol.isConcatSpreadable%](#sec-well-known-symbols)).
3.  If `spreadable` is not undefined, return
    [ToBoolean](#sec-toboolean)(`spreadable`).
4.  Return ? [IsArray](#sec-isarray)(`O`).

# <span class="secnum">23.1.3.3</span> Array.prototype.constructor

The initial value of `Array.prototype.constructor` is
[%Array%](#sec-array-constructor).

# <span class="secnum">23.1.3.4</span> Array.prototype.copyWithin ( `target`, `start` \[ , `end` \] )

<span class="note">Note 1</span>

<div class="note-contents">

The `end` argument is optional. If it is not provided, the length of the
this value is used.

</div>

<span class="note">Note 2</span>

<div class="note-contents">

If `target` is negative, it is treated as `length` + `target` where
`length` is the length of the array. If `start` is negative, it is
treated as `length` + `start`. If `end` is negative, it is treated as
`length` + `end`.

</div>

This method performs the following steps when called:

1.  Let `O` be ? [ToObject](#sec-toobject)(this value).
2.  Let `len` be ? <a href="#sec-lengthofarraylike"
    class="e-user-code">LengthOfArrayLike</a>(`O`).
3.  Let `relativeTarget` be ? <a href="#sec-tointegerorinfinity"
    class="e-user-code">ToIntegerOrInfinity</a>(`target`).
4.  If `relativeTarget` = -∞, let `to` be 0.
5.  Else if `relativeTarget` \< 0, let `to` be [max](#eqn-max)(`len` +
    `relativeTarget`, 0).
6.  Else, let `to` be [min](#eqn-min)(`relativeTarget`, `len`).
7.  Let `relativeStart` be ? <a href="#sec-tointegerorinfinity"
    class="e-user-code">ToIntegerOrInfinity</a>(`start`).
8.  If `relativeStart` = -∞, let `from` be 0.
9.  Else if `relativeStart` \< 0, let `from` be [max](#eqn-max)(`len` +
    `relativeStart`, 0).
10. Else, let `from` be [min](#eqn-min)(`relativeStart`, `len`).
11. If `end` is undefined, let `relativeEnd` be `len`; else let
    `relativeEnd` be ? <a href="#sec-tointegerorinfinity"
    class="e-user-code">ToIntegerOrInfinity</a>(`end`).
12. If `relativeEnd` = -∞, let `final` be 0.
13. Else if `relativeEnd` \< 0, let `final` be [max](#eqn-max)(`len` +
    `relativeEnd`, 0).
14. Else, let `final` be [min](#eqn-min)(`relativeEnd`, `len`).
15. Let `count` be [min](#eqn-min)(`final` - `from`, `len` - `to`).
16. If `from` \< `to` and `to` \< `from` + `count`, then
    1.  Let `direction` be -1.
    2.  Set `from` to `from` + `count` - 1.
    3.  Set `to` to `to` + `count` - 1.
17. Else,
    1.  Let `direction` be 1.
18. Repeat, while `count` \> 0,
    1.  Let `fromKey` be ! [ToString](#sec-tostring)([𝔽](#𝔽)(`from`)).
    2.  Let `toKey` be ! [ToString](#sec-tostring)([𝔽](#𝔽)(`to`)).
    3.  Let `fromPresent` be
        ? <a href="#sec-hasproperty" class="e-user-code">HasProperty</a>(`O`,
        `fromKey`).
    4.  If `fromPresent` is true, then
        1.  Let `fromValue` be
            ? <a href="#sec-get-o-p" class="e-user-code">Get</a>(`O`,
            `fromKey`).
        2.  Perform
            ? <a href="#sec-set-o-p-v-throw" class="e-user-code">Set</a>(`O`,
            `toKey`, `fromValue`, true).
    5.  Else,
        1.  [Assert](#assert): `fromPresent` is false.
        2.  Perform ? <a href="#sec-deletepropertyorthrow"
            class="e-user-code">DeletePropertyOrThrow</a>(`O`, `toKey`).
    6.  Set `from` to `from` + `direction`.
    7.  Set `to` to `to` + `direction`.
    8.  Set `count` to `count` - 1.
19. Return `O`.

<span class="note">Note 3</span>

<div class="note-contents">

This method is intentionally generic; it does not require that its this
value be an Array. Therefore it can be transferred to other kinds of
objects for use as a method.

</div>

# <span class="secnum">23.1.3.5</span> Array.prototype.entries ( )

This method performs the following steps when called:

1.  Let `O` be ? [ToObject](#sec-toobject)(this value).
2.  Return [CreateArrayIterator](#sec-createarrayiterator)(`O`,
    key+value).

# <span class="secnum">23.1.3.6</span> Array.prototype.every ( `callback` \[ , `thisArg` \] )

<span class="note">Note 1</span>

<div class="note-contents">

`callback` should be a function that accepts three arguments and returns
a value that is coercible to a Boolean value. `every` calls `callback`
once for each element present in the array, in ascending order, until it
finds one where `callback` returns false. If such an element is found,
`every` immediately returns false. Otherwise, `every` returns true.
`callback` is called only for elements of the array which actually
exist; it is not called for missing elements of the array.

If a `thisArg` parameter is provided, it will be used as the this value
for each invocation of `callback`. If it is not provided, undefined is
used instead.

`callback` is called with three arguments: the value of the element, the
index of the element, and the object being traversed.

`every` does not directly mutate the object on which it is called but
the object may be mutated by the calls to `callback`.

The range of elements processed by `every` is set before the first call
to `callback`. Elements which are appended to the array after the call
to `every` begins will not be visited by `callback`. If existing
elements of the array are changed, their value as passed to `callback`
will be the value at the time `every` visits them; elements that are
deleted after the call to `every` begins and before being visited are
not visited. `every` acts like the "for all" quantifier in mathematics.
In particular, for an empty array, it returns true.

</div>

This method performs the following steps when called:

1.  Let `O` be ? [ToObject](#sec-toobject)(this value).
2.  Let `len` be ? <a href="#sec-lengthofarraylike"
    class="e-user-code">LengthOfArrayLike</a>(`O`).
3.  If [IsCallable](#sec-iscallable)(`callback`) is false, throw a
    TypeError exception.
4.  Let `k` be 0.
5.  Repeat, while `k` \< `len`,
    1.  Let `Pk` be ! [ToString](#sec-tostring)([𝔽](#𝔽)(`k`)).
    2.  Let `kPresent` be
        ? <a href="#sec-hasproperty" class="e-user-code">HasProperty</a>(`O`,
        `Pk`).
    3.  If `kPresent` is true, then
        1.  Let `kValue` be
            ? <a href="#sec-get-o-p" class="e-user-code">Get</a>(`O`,
            `Pk`).
        2.  Let `testResult` be [ToBoolean](#sec-toboolean)(?
            <a href="#sec-call" class="e-user-code">Call</a>(`callback`,
            `thisArg`, « `kValue`, [𝔽](#𝔽)(`k`), `O` »)).
        3.  If `testResult` is false, return false.
    4.  Set `k` to `k` + 1.
6.  Return true.

<span class="note">Note 2</span>

<div class="note-contents">

This method is intentionally generic; it does not require that its this
value be an Array. Therefore it can be transferred to other kinds of
objects for use as a method.

</div>

# <span class="secnum">23.1.3.7</span> Array.prototype.fill ( `value` \[ , `start` \[ , `end` \] \] )

<span class="note">Note 1</span>

<div class="note-contents">

The `start` argument is optional. If it is not provided, +0<sub>𝔽</sub>
is used.

The `end` argument is optional. If it is not provided, the length of the
this value is used.

</div>

<span class="note">Note 2</span>

<div class="note-contents">

If `start` is negative, it is treated as `length` + `start` where
`length` is the length of the array. If `end` is negative, it is treated
as `length` + `end`.

</div>

This method performs the following steps when called:

1.  Let `O` be ? [ToObject](#sec-toobject)(this value).
2.  Let `len` be ? <a href="#sec-lengthofarraylike"
    class="e-user-code">LengthOfArrayLike</a>(`O`).
3.  Let `relativeStart` be ? <a href="#sec-tointegerorinfinity"
    class="e-user-code">ToIntegerOrInfinity</a>(`start`).
4.  If `relativeStart` = -∞, let `k` be 0.
5.  Else if `relativeStart` \< 0, let `k` be [max](#eqn-max)(`len` +
    `relativeStart`, 0).
6.  Else, let `k` be [min](#eqn-min)(`relativeStart`, `len`).
7.  If `end` is undefined, let `relativeEnd` be `len`; else let
    `relativeEnd` be ? <a href="#sec-tointegerorinfinity"
    class="e-user-code">ToIntegerOrInfinity</a>(`end`).
8.  If `relativeEnd` = -∞, let `final` be 0.
9.  Else if `relativeEnd` \< 0, let `final` be [max](#eqn-max)(`len` +
    `relativeEnd`, 0).
10. Else, let `final` be [min](#eqn-min)(`relativeEnd`, `len`).
11. Repeat, while `k` \< `final`,
    1.  Let `Pk` be ! [ToString](#sec-tostring)([𝔽](#𝔽)(`k`)).
    2.  Perform
        ? <a href="#sec-set-o-p-v-throw" class="e-user-code">Set</a>(`O`,
        `Pk`, `value`, true).
    3.  Set `k` to `k` + 1.
12. Return `O`.

<span class="note">Note 3</span>

<div class="note-contents">

This method is intentionally generic; it does not require that its this
value be an Array. Therefore it can be transferred to other kinds of
objects for use as a method.

</div>

# <span class="secnum">23.1.3.8</span> Array.prototype.filter ( `callback` \[ , `thisArg` \] )

<span class="note">Note 1</span>

<div class="note-contents">

`callback` should be a function that accepts three arguments and returns
a value that is coercible to a Boolean value. `filter` calls `callback`
once for each element in the array, in ascending order, and constructs a
new array of all the values for which `callback` returns true.
`callback` is called only for elements of the array which actually
exist; it is not called for missing elements of the array.

If a `thisArg` parameter is provided, it will be used as the this value
for each invocation of `callback`. If it is not provided, undefined is
used instead.

`callback` is called with three arguments: the value of the element, the
index of the element, and the object being traversed.

`filter` does not directly mutate the object on which it is called but
the object may be mutated by the calls to `callback`.

The range of elements processed by `filter` is set before the first call
to `callback`. Elements which are appended to the array after the call
to `filter` begins will not be visited by `callback`. If existing
elements of the array are changed their value as passed to `callback`
will be the value at the time `filter` visits them; elements that are
deleted after the call to `filter` begins and before being visited are
not visited.

</div>

This method performs the following steps when called:

1.  Let `O` be ? [ToObject](#sec-toobject)(this value).
2.  Let `len` be ? <a href="#sec-lengthofarraylike"
    class="e-user-code">LengthOfArrayLike</a>(`O`).
3.  If [IsCallable](#sec-iscallable)(`callback`) is false, throw a
    TypeError exception.
4.  Let `A` be ? <a href="#sec-arrayspeciescreate"
    class="e-user-code">ArraySpeciesCreate</a>(`O`, 0).
5.  Let `k` be 0.
6.  Let `to` be 0.
7.  Repeat, while `k` \< `len`,
    1.  Let `Pk` be ! [ToString](#sec-tostring)([𝔽](#𝔽)(`k`)).
    2.  Let `kPresent` be
        ? <a href="#sec-hasproperty" class="e-user-code">HasProperty</a>(`O`,
        `Pk`).
    3.  If `kPresent` is true, then
        1.  Let `kValue` be
            ? <a href="#sec-get-o-p" class="e-user-code">Get</a>(`O`,
            `Pk`).
        2.  Let `selected` be [ToBoolean](#sec-toboolean)(?
            <a href="#sec-call" class="e-user-code">Call</a>(`callback`,
            `thisArg`, « `kValue`, [𝔽](#𝔽)(`k`), `O` »)).
        3.  If `selected` is true, then
            1.  Perform ? <a href="#sec-createdatapropertyorthrow"
                class="e-user-code">CreateDataPropertyOrThrow</a>(`A`,
                ! [ToString](#sec-tostring)([𝔽](#𝔽)(`to`)), `kValue`).
            2.  Set `to` to `to` + 1.
    4.  Set `k` to `k` + 1.
8.  Return `A`.

<span class="note">Note 2</span>

<div class="note-contents">

This method is intentionally generic; it does not require that its this
value be an Array. Therefore it can be transferred to other kinds of
objects for use as a method.

</div>

# <span class="secnum">23.1.3.9</span> Array.prototype.find ( `predicate` \[ , `thisArg` \] )

<span class="note">Note 1</span>

<div class="note-contents">

This method calls `predicate` once for each element of the array, in
ascending index order, until it finds one where `predicate` returns a
value that coerces to true. If such an element is found, `find`
immediately returns that element value. Otherwise, `find` returns
undefined.

See [FindViaPredicate](#sec-findviapredicate) for additional
information.

</div>

This method performs the following steps when called:

1.  Let `O` be ? [ToObject](#sec-toobject)(this value).
2.  Let `len` be ? <a href="#sec-lengthofarraylike"
    class="e-user-code">LengthOfArrayLike</a>(`O`).
3.  Let `findRec` be
    ? <a href="#sec-findviapredicate" class="e-user-code">FindViaPredicate</a>(`O`,
    `len`, ascending, `predicate`, `thisArg`).
4.  Return `findRec`.`[[Value]]`.

<span class="note">Note 2</span>

<div class="note-contents">

This method is intentionally generic; it does not require that its this
value be an Array. Therefore it can be transferred to other kinds of
objects for use as a method.

</div>

# <span class="secnum">23.1.3.10</span> Array.prototype.findIndex ( `predicate` \[ , `thisArg` \] )

<span class="note">Note 1</span>

<div class="note-contents">

This method calls `predicate` once for each element of the array, in
ascending index order, until it finds one where `predicate` returns a
value that coerces to true. If such an element is found, `findIndex`
immediately returns the index of that element value. Otherwise,
`findIndex` returns -1.

See [FindViaPredicate](#sec-findviapredicate) for additional
information.

</div>

This method performs the following steps when called:

1.  Let `O` be ? [ToObject](#sec-toobject)(this value).
2.  Let `len` be ? <a href="#sec-lengthofarraylike"
    class="e-user-code">LengthOfArrayLike</a>(`O`).
3.  Let `findRec` be
    ? <a href="#sec-findviapredicate" class="e-user-code">FindViaPredicate</a>(`O`,
    `len`, ascending, `predicate`, `thisArg`).
4.  Return `findRec`.`[[Index]]`.

<span class="note">Note 2</span>

<div class="note-contents">

This method is intentionally generic; it does not require that its this
value be an Array. Therefore it can be transferred to other kinds of
objects for use as a method.

</div>

# <span class="secnum">23.1.3.11</span> Array.prototype.findLast ( `predicate` \[ , `thisArg` \] )

<span class="note">Note 1</span>

<div class="note-contents">

This method calls `predicate` once for each element of the array, in

value that coerces to true. If such an element is found, `findLast`
immediately returns that element value. Otherwise, `findLast` returns
undefined.

See [FindViaPredicate](#sec-findviapredicate) for additional
information.

</div>

This method performs the following steps when called:

2.  Let `len` be ? <a href="#sec-lengthofarraylike"
    class="e-user-code">LengthOfArrayLike</a>(`O`).
3.  Let `findRec` be

This method is intentionally generic; it does not require that its this

# <span class="secnum">23.1.3.12</span> Array.prototype.findLastIndex ( `predicate` \[ , `thisArg` \] )

<span class="note">Note 1</span>

<div class="note-contents">

This method calls `predicate` once for each element of the array, in

immediately returns the index of that element value. Otherwise,
`findLastIndex` returns -1.

See [FindViaPredicate](#sec-findviapredicate) for additional
information.

</div>

This method performs the following steps when called:

3.  Let `findRec` be
    ? <a href="#sec-findviapredicate" class="e-user-code">FindViaPredicate</a>(`O`,
    `len`, descending, `predicate`, `thisArg`).

<span class="note">Note 2</span>

<div class="note-contents">

This method is intentionally generic; it does not require that its this

# <span class="secnum">23.1.3.12.1</span> FindViaPredicate ( `O`, `len`, `direction`, `predicate`, `thisArg` )

The abstract operation FindViaPredicate takes arguments `O` (an Object),
`len` (a non-negative [integer](#integer)), `direction` (ascending or
descending), `predicate` (an [ECMAScript language
value](#sec-ecmascript-language-types)), and `thisArg` (an [ECMAScript
language value](#sec-ecmascript-language-types)) and returns either a
[normal completion
containing](#sec-completion-record-specification-type) a
[Record](#sec-list-and-record-specification-type) with fields
`[[Index]]` (an [integral Number](#integral-number)) and `[[Value]]` (an
[ECMAScript language value](#sec-ecmascript-language-types)) or a [throw
completion](#sec-completion-record-specification-type).

`O` should be an [array-like object](#sec-lengthofarraylike) or a
[TypedArray](#typedarray). This operation calls `predicate` once for
each element of `O`, in either ascending index order or descending index
order (as indicated by `direction`), until it finds one where
`predicate` returns a value that coerces to true. At that point, this
operation returns a [Record](#sec-list-and-record-specification-type)
that gives the index and value of the element found. If no such element
is found, this operation returns a
[Record](#sec-list-and-record-specification-type) that specifies
-1<sub>𝔽</sub> for the index and undefined for the value.

`predicate` should be a function. When called for an element of the
array, it is passed three arguments: the value of the element, the index
of the element, and the object being traversed. Its return value will be
coerced to a Boolean value.

`thisArg` will be used as the this value for each invocation of
`predicate`.

This operation does not directly mutate the object on which it is
called, but the object may be mutated by the calls to `predicate`.

The range of elements processed is set before the first call to
`predicate`, just before the traversal begins. Elements that are
appended to the array after this will not be visited by `predicate`. If
existing elements of the array are changed, their value as passed to
`predicate` will be the value at the time that this operation visits
them. Elements that are deleted after traversal begins and before being
visited are still visited and are either looked up from the prototype or
are undefined.

It performs the following steps when called:

1.  If [IsCallable](#sec-iscallable)(`predicate`) is false, throw a
    TypeError exception.
2.  If `direction` is ascending, then
    1.  Let `indices` be a
        [List](#sec-list-and-record-specification-type) of the
        [integers](#integer) in the [interval](#interval) from 0
        (inclusive) to `len` (exclusive), in ascending order.
3.  Else,
    1.  Let `indices` be a
        [List](#sec-list-and-record-specification-type) of the
        [integers](#integer) in the [interval](#interval) from 0
        (inclusive) to `len` (exclusive), in descending order.
4.  For each [integer](#integer) `k` of `indices`, do
    1.  Let `Pk` be ! [ToString](#sec-tostring)([𝔽](#𝔽)(`k`)).
    2.  [NOTE](#note-step): If `O` is a [TypedArray](#typedarray), the
        following invocation of [Get](#sec-get-o-p) will return a
        [normal completion](#sec-completion-record-specification-type).
    3.  Let `kValue` be
        ? <a href="#sec-get-o-p" class="e-user-code">Get</a>(`O`, `Pk`).
    4.  Let `testResult` be
        ? <a href="#sec-call" class="e-user-code">Call</a>(`predicate`,
        `thisArg`, « `kValue`, [𝔽](#𝔽)(`k`), `O` »).
    5.  If [ToBoolean](#sec-toboolean)(`testResult`) is true, return the
        [Record](#sec-list-and-record-specification-type) { `[[Index]]`:
        [𝔽](#𝔽)(`k`), `[[Value]]`: `kValue` }.
5.  Return the [Record](#sec-list-and-record-specification-type) {
    `[[Index]]`: -1<sub>𝔽</sub>, `[[Value]]`: undefined }.

# <span class="secnum">23.1.3.13</span> Array.prototype.flat ( \[ `depth` \] )

This method performs the following steps when called:

1.  Let `O` be ? [ToObject](#sec-toobject)(this value).
2.  Let `sourceLen` be ? <a href="#sec-lengthofarraylike"
    class="e-user-code">LengthOfArrayLike</a>(`O`).
3.  Let `depthNum` be 1.
4.  If `depth` is not undefined, then
    1.  Set `depthNum` to ? <a href="#sec-tointegerorinfinity"
        class="e-user-code">ToIntegerOrInfinity</a>(`depth`).
    2.  If `depthNum` \< 0, set `depthNum` to 0.
5.  Let `A` be ? <a href="#sec-arrayspeciescreate"
    class="e-user-code">ArraySpeciesCreate</a>(`O`, 0).
6.  Perform
    ? <a href="#sec-flattenintoarray" class="e-user-code">FlattenIntoArray</a>(`A`,
    `O`, `sourceLen`, 0, `depthNum`).
7.  Return `A`.

# <span class="secnum">23.1.3.13.1</span> FlattenIntoArray ( `target`, `source`, `sourceLen`, `start`, `depth` \[ , `mapperFunction` \[ , `thisArg` \] \] )

The abstract operation FlattenIntoArray takes arguments `target` (an
Object), `source` (an Object), `sourceLen` (a non-negative
[integer](#integer)), `start` (a non-negative [integer](#integer)), and
`depth` (a non-negative [integer](#integer) or +∞) and optional
arguments `mapperFunction` (a [function object](#function-object)) and
`thisArg` (an [ECMAScript language
value](#sec-ecmascript-language-types)) and returns either a [normal
completion containing](#sec-completion-record-specification-type) a
non-negative [integer](#integer) or a [throw
completion](#sec-completion-record-specification-type). It performs the
following steps when called:

1.  [Assert](#assert): If `mapperFunction` is present, then
    [IsCallable](#sec-iscallable)(`mapperFunction`) is true, `thisArg`
    is present, and `depth` is 1.
2.  Let `targetIndex` be `start`.
3.  Let `sourceIndex` be +0<sub>𝔽</sub>.
4.  Repeat, while [ℝ](#ℝ)(`sourceIndex`) \< `sourceLen`,
    1.  Let `P` be ! [ToString](#sec-tostring)(`sourceIndex`).
    2.  Let `exists` be
        ? <a href="#sec-hasproperty" class="e-user-code">HasProperty</a>(`source`,
        `P`).
    3.  If `exists` is true, then
        1.  Let `element` be
            ? <a href="#sec-get-o-p" class="e-user-code">Get</a>(`source`,
            `P`).
        2.  If `mapperFunction` is present, then
            1.  Set `element` to
                ? <a href="#sec-call" class="e-user-code">Call</a>(`mapperFunction`,
                `thisArg`, « `element`, `sourceIndex`, `source` »).
        3.  Let `shouldFlatten` be false.
        4.  If `depth` \> 0, then
            1.  Set `shouldFlatten` to
                ? [IsArray](#sec-isarray)(`element`).
        5.  If `shouldFlatten` is true, then
            1.  If `depth` = +∞, let `newDepth` be +∞.
            2.  Else, let `newDepth` be `depth` - 1.
            3.  Let `elementLen` be ? <a href="#sec-lengthofarraylike"
                class="e-user-code">LengthOfArrayLike</a>(`element`).
            4.  Set `targetIndex` to
                ? <a href="#sec-flattenintoarray" class="e-user-code">FlattenIntoArray</a>(`target`,
                `element`, `elementLen`, `targetIndex`, `newDepth`).
        6.  Else,
            1.  If `targetIndex` ≥ 2<sup>53</sup> - 1, throw a TypeError
                exception.
            2.  Perform ? <a href="#sec-createdatapropertyorthrow"
                class="e-user-code">CreateDataPropertyOrThrow</a>(`target`,
                ! [ToString](#sec-tostring)([𝔽](#𝔽)(`targetIndex`)),
                `element`).
            3.  Set `targetIndex` to `targetIndex` + 1.
    4.  Set `sourceIndex` to `sourceIndex` + 1<sub>𝔽</sub>.
5.  Return `targetIndex`.

# <span class="secnum">23.1.3.14</span> Array.prototype.flatMap ( `mapperFunction` \[ , `thisArg` \] )

This method performs the following steps when called:

1.  Let `O` be ? [ToObject](#sec-toobject)(this value).
2.  Let `sourceLen` be ? <a href="#sec-lengthofarraylike"
    class="e-user-code">LengthOfArrayLike</a>(`O`).
3.  If [IsCallable](#sec-iscallable)(`mapperFunction`) is false, throw a
    TypeError exception.
4.  Let `A` be ? <a href="#sec-arrayspeciescreate"
    class="e-user-code">ArraySpeciesCreate</a>(`O`, 0).
5.  Perform
    ? <a href="#sec-flattenintoarray" class="e-user-code">FlattenIntoArray</a>(`A`,
    `O`, `sourceLen`, 0, 1, `mapperFunction`, `thisArg`).
6.  Return `A`.

# <span class="secnum">23.1.3.15</span> Array.prototype.forEach ( `callback` \[ , `thisArg` \] )

<span class="note">Note 1</span>

<div class="note-contents">

`callback` should be a function that accepts three arguments. `forEach`
calls `callback` once for each element present in the array, in
ascending order. `callback` is called only for elements of the array
which actually exist; it is not called for missing elements of the
array.

If a `thisArg` parameter is provided, it will be used as the this value
for each invocation of `callback`. If it is not provided, undefined is
used instead.

`callback` is called with three arguments: the value of the element, the
index of the element, and the object being traversed.

`forEach` does not directly mutate the object on which it is called but
the object may be mutated by the calls to `callback`.

The range of elements processed by `forEach` is set before the first
call to `callback`. Elements which are appended to the array after the
call to `forEach` begins will not be visited by `callback`. If existing
elements of the array are changed, their value as passed to `callback`
will be the value at the time `forEach` visits them; elements that are
deleted after the call to `forEach` begins and before being visited are
not visited.

</div>

This method performs the following steps when called:

1.  Let `O` be ? [ToObject](#sec-toobject)(this value).
2.  Let `len` be ? <a href="#sec-lengthofarraylike"
    class="e-user-code">LengthOfArrayLike</a>(`O`).
3.  If [IsCallable](#sec-iscallable)(`callback`) is false, throw a
    TypeError exception.
4.  Let `k` be 0.
5.  Repeat, while `k` \< `len`,
    1.  Let `Pk` be ! [ToString](#sec-tostring)([𝔽](#𝔽)(`k`)).
    2.  Let `kPresent` be
        ? <a href="#sec-hasproperty" class="e-user-code">HasProperty</a>(`O`,
        `Pk`).
    3.  If `kPresent` is true, then
        1.  Let `kValue` be
            ? <a href="#sec-get-o-p" class="e-user-code">Get</a>(`O`,
            `Pk`).
        2.  Perform
            ? <a href="#sec-call" class="e-user-code">Call</a>(`callback`,
            `thisArg`, « `kValue`, [𝔽](#𝔽)(`k`), `O` »).
    4.  Set `k` to `k` + 1.
6.  Return undefined.

<span class="note">Note 2</span>

<div class="note-contents">

This method is intentionally generic; it does not require that its this
value be an Array. Therefore it can be transferred to other kinds of
objects for use as a method.

</div>

# <span class="secnum">23.1.3.16</span> Array.prototype.includes ( `searchElement` \[ , `fromIndex` \] )

<span class="note">Note 1</span>

<div class="note-contents">

This method compares `searchElement` to the elements of the array, in
ascending order, using the [SameValueZero](#sec-samevaluezero)
algorithm, and if found at any position, returns true; otherwise, it
returns false.

The optional second argument `fromIndex` defaults to +0<sub>𝔽</sub>
(i.e. the whole array is searched). If it is greater than or equal to
the length of the array, false is returned, i.e. the array will not be
searched. If it is less than -0<sub>𝔽</sub>, it is used as the offset
from the end of the array to compute `fromIndex`. If the computed index
is less than or equal to +0<sub>𝔽</sub>, the whole array will be
searched.

</div>

This method performs the following steps when called:

1.  Let `O` be ? [ToObject](#sec-toobject)(this value).
2.  Let `len` be ? <a href="#sec-lengthofarraylike"
    class="e-user-code">LengthOfArrayLike</a>(`O`).
3.  If `len` = 0, return false.
4.  Let `n` be ? <a href="#sec-tointegerorinfinity"
    class="e-user-code">ToIntegerOrInfinity</a>(`fromIndex`).
5.  [Assert](#assert): If `fromIndex` is undefined, then `n` is 0.
6.  If `n` = +∞, return false.
7.  If `n` = -∞, set `n` to 0.
8.  If `n` ≥ 0, then
    1.  Let `k` be `n`.
9.  Else,
    1.  Let `k` be `len` + `n`.
    2.  If `k` \< 0, set `k` to 0.
10. Repeat, while `k` \< `len`,
    1.  Let `elementK` be
        ? <a href="#sec-get-o-p" class="e-user-code">Get</a>(`O`,
        ! [ToString](#sec-tostring)([𝔽](#𝔽)(`k`))).
    2.  If [SameValueZero](#sec-samevaluezero)(`searchElement`,
        `elementK`) is true, return true.
    3.  Set `k` to `k` + 1.
11. Return false.

<span class="note">Note 2</span>

<div class="note-contents">

This method is intentionally generic; it does not require that its this
value be an Array. Therefore it can be transferred to other kinds of
objects for use as a method.

</div>

<span class="note">Note 3</span>

<div class="note-contents">

This method intentionally differs from the similar `indexOf` method in
two ways. First, it uses the [SameValueZero](#sec-samevaluezero)
algorithm, instead of [IsStrictlyEqual](#sec-isstrictlyequal), allowing
it to detect NaN array elements. Second, it does not skip missing array
elements, instead treating them as undefined.

</div>

# <span class="secnum">23.1.3.17</span> Array.prototype.indexOf ( `searchElement` \[ , `fromIndex` \] )

This method compares `searchElement` to the elements of the array, in
ascending order, using the [IsStrictlyEqual](#sec-isstrictlyequal)
algorithm, and if found at one or more indices, returns the smallest
such index; otherwise, it returns -1<sub>𝔽</sub>.

<span class="note">Note 1</span>

<div class="note-contents">

The optional second argument `fromIndex` defaults to +0<sub>𝔽</sub>
(i.e. the whole array is searched). If it is greater than or equal to
the length of the array, -1<sub>𝔽</sub> is returned, i.e. the array will
not be searched. If it is less than -0<sub>𝔽</sub>, it is used to
compute an offset from the end of the array. If the computed index is
less than or equal to +0<sub>𝔽</sub>, the whole array will be searched.

</div>

This method performs the following steps when called:

1.  Let `O` be ? [ToObject](#sec-toobject)(this value).
2.  Let `len` be ? <a href="#sec-lengthofarraylike"
    class="e-user-code">LengthOfArrayLike</a>(`O`).
3.  If `len` = 0, return -1<sub>𝔽</sub>.
4.  Let `n` be ? <a href="#sec-tointegerorinfinity"
    class="e-user-code">ToIntegerOrInfinity</a>(`fromIndex`).
5.  [Assert](#assert): If `fromIndex` is undefined, then `n` is 0.
6.  If `n` = +∞, return -1<sub>𝔽</sub>.
7.  If `n` = -∞, set `n` to 0.
8.  If `n` ≥ 0, then
    1.  Let `k` be `n`.
9.  Else,
    1.  Let `k` be `len` + `n`.
    2.  If `k` \< 0, set `k` to 0.
10. Repeat, while `k` \< `len`,
    1.  Let `Pk` be ! [ToString](#sec-tostring)([𝔽](#𝔽)(`k`)).
    2.  Let `kPresent` be
        ? <a href="#sec-hasproperty" class="e-user-code">HasProperty</a>(`O`,
        `Pk`).
    3.  If `kPresent` is true, then
        1.  Let `elementK` be
            ? <a href="#sec-get-o-p" class="e-user-code">Get</a>(`O`,
            `Pk`).
        2.  If [IsStrictlyEqual](#sec-isstrictlyequal)(`searchElement`,
            `elementK`) is true, return [𝔽](#𝔽)(`k`).
    4.  Set `k` to `k` + 1.
11. Return -1<sub>𝔽</sub>.

<span class="note">Note 2</span>

<div class="note-contents">

This method is intentionally generic; it does not require that its this
value be an Array. Therefore it can be transferred to other kinds of
objects for use as a method.

</div>

# <span class="secnum">23.1.3.18</span> Array.prototype.join ( `separator` )

This method converts the elements of the array to Strings, and then
concatenates these Strings, separated by occurrences of the `separator`.
If no separator is provided, a single comma is used as the separator.

It performs the following steps when called:

1.  Let `O` be ? [ToObject](#sec-toobject)(this value).
2.  Let `len` be ? <a href="#sec-lengthofarraylike"
    class="e-user-code">LengthOfArrayLike</a>(`O`).
3.  If `separator` is undefined, let `sep` be ",".
4.  Else, let `sep` be
    ? <a href="#sec-tostring" class="e-user-code">ToString</a>(`separator`).
5.  Let `R` be the empty String.
6.  Let `k` be 0.
7.  Repeat, while `k` \< `len`,
    1.  If `k` \> 0, set `R` to the
        [string-concatenation](#string-concatenation) of `R` and `sep`.
    2.  Let `element` be
        ? <a href="#sec-get-o-p" class="e-user-code">Get</a>(`O`,
        ! [ToString](#sec-tostring)([𝔽](#𝔽)(`k`))).
    3.  If `element` is neither undefined nor null, then
        1.  Let `S` be
            ? <a href="#sec-tostring" class="e-user-code">ToString</a>(`element`).
        2.  Set `R` to the [string-concatenation](#string-concatenation)
            of `R` and `S`.
    4.  Set `k` to `k` + 1.
8.  Return `R`.

<span class="note">Note</span>

<div class="note-contents">

This method is intentionally generic; it does not require that its this
value be an Array. Therefore, it can be transferred to other kinds of
objects for use as a method.

</div>

2.  Return [CreateArrayIterator](#sec-createarrayiterator)(`O`, key).

# <span class="secnum">23.1.3.20</span> Array.prototype.lastIndexOf ( `searchElement` \[ , `fromIndex` \] )

<span class="note">Note 1</span>

<div class="note-contents">

This method compares `searchElement` to the elements of the array in
descending order using the [IsStrictlyEqual](#sec-isstrictlyequal)
algorithm, and if found at one or more indices, returns the largest such
index; otherwise, it returns -1<sub>𝔽</sub>.

The optional second argument `fromIndex` defaults to the array's length
minus one (i.e. the whole array is searched). If it is greater than or
equal to the length of the array, the whole array will be searched. If
it is less than -0<sub>𝔽</sub>, it is used to compute an offset from the
end of the array. If the computed index is less than -0<sub>𝔽</sub>,
-1<sub>𝔽</sub> is returned.

</div>

This method performs the following steps when called:

1.  Let `O` be ? [ToObject](#sec-toobject)(this value).
2.  Let `len` be ? <a href="#sec-lengthofarraylike"
    class="e-user-code">LengthOfArrayLike</a>(`O`).
3.  If `len` = 0, return -1<sub>𝔽</sub>.
4.  If `fromIndex` is present, let `n` be
    ? <a href="#sec-tointegerorinfinity"
    class="e-user-code">ToIntegerOrInfinity</a>(`fromIndex`); else let
    `n` be `len` - 1.
5.  If `n` = -∞, return -1<sub>𝔽</sub>.
6.  If `n` ≥ 0, then
    1.  Let `k` be [min](#eqn-min)(`n`, `len` - 1).
7.  Else,
    1.  Let `k` be `len` + `n`.
8.  Repeat, while `k` ≥ 0,
    1.  Let `Pk` be ! [ToString](#sec-tostring)([𝔽](#𝔽)(`k`)).
    2.  Let `kPresent` be
        ? <a href="#sec-hasproperty" class="e-user-code">HasProperty</a>(`O`,
        `Pk`).
    3.  If `kPresent` is true, then
        1.  Let `elementK` be
            ? <a href="#sec-get-o-p" class="e-user-code">Get</a>(`O`,
            `Pk`).
        2.  If [IsStrictlyEqual](#sec-isstrictlyequal)(`searchElement`,
            `elementK`) is true, return [𝔽](#𝔽)(`k`).
    4.  Set `k` to `k` - 1.
9.  Return -1<sub>𝔽</sub>.

<span class="note">Note 2</span>

<div class="note-contents">

This method is intentionally generic; it does not require that its this
value be an Array. Therefore it can be transferred to other kinds of
objects for use as a method.

</div>

# <span class="secnum">23.1.3.21</span> Array.prototype.map ( `callback` \[ , `thisArg` \] )

<span class="note">Note 1</span>

<div class="note-contents">

`callback` should be a function that accepts three arguments. `map`
calls `callback` once for each element in the array, in ascending order,
and constructs a new Array from the results. `callback` is called only
for elements of the array which actually exist; it is not called for
missing elements of the array.

If a `thisArg` parameter is provided, it will be used as the this value
for each invocation of `callback`. If it is not provided, undefined is
used instead.

`callback` is called with three arguments: the value of the element, the
index of the element, and the object being traversed.

`map` does not directly mutate the object on which it is called but the
object may be mutated by the calls to `callback`.

The range of elements processed by `map` is set before the first call to
`callback`. Elements which are appended to the array after the call to
`map` begins will not be visited by `callback`. If existing elements of
the array are changed, their value as passed to `callback` will be the
value at the time `map` visits them; elements that are deleted after the
call to `map` begins and before being visited are not visited.

</div>

This method performs the following steps when called:

1.  Let `O` be ? [ToObject](#sec-toobject)(this value).
2.  Let `len` be ? <a href="#sec-lengthofarraylike"
    class="e-user-code">LengthOfArrayLike</a>(`O`).
3.  If [IsCallable](#sec-iscallable)(`callback`) is false, throw a
    TypeError exception.
4.  Let `A` be ? <a href="#sec-arrayspeciescreate"
    class="e-user-code">ArraySpeciesCreate</a>(`O`, `len`).
5.  Let `k` be 0.
6.  Repeat, while `k` \< `len`,
    1.  Let `Pk` be ! [ToString](#sec-tostring)([𝔽](#𝔽)(`k`)).
    2.  Let `kPresent` be
        ? <a href="#sec-hasproperty" class="e-user-code">HasProperty</a>(`O`,
        `Pk`).
    3.  If `kPresent` is true, then
        1.  Let `kValue` be
            ? <a href="#sec-get-o-p" class="e-user-code">Get</a>(`O`,
            `Pk`).
        2.  Let `mappedValue` be
            ? <a href="#sec-call" class="e-user-code">Call</a>(`callback`,
            `thisArg`, « `kValue`, [𝔽](#𝔽)(`k`), `O` »).
        3.  Perform ? <a href="#sec-createdatapropertyorthrow"
            class="e-user-code">CreateDataPropertyOrThrow</a>(`A`, `Pk`,
            `mappedValue`).
    4.  Set `k` to `k` + 1.
7.  Return `A`.

<span class="note">Note 2</span>

<div class="note-contents">

This method is intentionally generic; it does not require that its this
value be an Array. Therefore it can be transferred to other kinds of
objects for use as a method.

# <span class="secnum">23.1.3.22</span> Array.prototype.pop ( )

<span class="note">Note 1</span>

<div class="note-contents">

This method removes the last element of the array and returns it.

</div>

This method performs the following steps when called:

1.  Let `O` be ? [ToObject](#sec-toobject)(this value).
2.  Let `len` be ? <a href="#sec-lengthofarraylike"
    class="e-user-code">LengthOfArrayLike</a>(`O`).

    1.  Perform
        ? <a href="#sec-set-o-p-v-throw" class="e-user-code">Set</a>(`O`,

4.  [Assert](#assert): `len` \> 0.
5.  Let `newLen` be [𝔽](#𝔽)(`len` - 1).
6.  Let `index` be ! [ToString](#sec-tostring)(`newLen`).
7.  Let `element` be
    ? <a href="#sec-get-o-p" class="e-user-code">Get</a>(`O`, `index`).
8.  Perform ? <a href="#sec-deletepropertyorthrow"
    class="e-user-code">DeletePropertyOrThrow</a>(`O`, `index`).
9.  Perform
    ? <a href="#sec-set-o-p-v-throw" class="e-user-code">Set</a>(`O`,
    "length", `newLen`, true).
10. Return `element`.

# <span class="secnum">23.1.3.23</span> Array.prototype.push ( ...`items` )

<span class="note">Note 1</span>

<div class="note-contents">

This method appends the arguments to the end of the array, in the order
in which they appear. It returns the new length of the array.

</div>

This method performs the following steps when called:

1.  Let `O` be ? [ToObject](#sec-toobject)(this value).
2.  Let `len` be ? <a href="#sec-lengthofarraylike"
    class="e-user-code">LengthOfArrayLike</a>(`O`).
3.  Let `argCount` be the number of elements in `items`.
4.  If `len` + `argCount` \> 2<sup>53</sup> - 1, throw a TypeError
    exception.
5.  For each element `E` of `items`, do

        ? <a href="#sec-set-o-p-v-throw" class="e-user-code">Set</a>(`O`,
        ! [ToString](#sec-tostring)([𝔽](#𝔽)(`len`)), `E`, true).
    2.  Set `len` to `len` + 1.
6.  Perform
    ? <a href="#sec-set-o-p-v-throw" class="e-user-code">Set</a>(`O`,
    "length", [𝔽](#𝔽)(`len`), true).
7.  Return [𝔽](#𝔽)(`len`).

The "length" property of this method is 1<sub>𝔽</sub>.
